blocks.content: High Courts have administrative and judicial control over all subordinate courts within their jurisdiction.
High Courts have administrative and judicial control over all subordinate courts within their jurisdiction.

items: Article 227 covers both administrative AND judicial control, which is a frequent source of tricky multiple-choice questions.
High Court superintendence under Article 227 applies strictly to courts and tribunals within its specified territorial jurisdiction.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 227 grants High Courts the power of superintendence over all subordinate courts within their territorial limits.
The scope of control exercised by High Courts includes both administrative superintendence and judicial superintendence.
This power ensures uniform administration of justice and proper functioning of lower courts within the state.
